skills.name: oca-governance-pr-workflow
skills.title: OCA PR Workflow
skills.compact_rules:
OCA PR workflow. Replaces caveman-commit for OCA projects.
- Workflow: issue approved -> branch from ver -> implement -> commit OCA format -> PR with template -> CI + review
- Branch naming: {type}/{module}-{desc} with types: fix/, imp/, add/, ref/, mig/
- PR body must include: Description, Related Issue (Closes #N), OCA Compliance Checklist
- Checklist: version format, license AGPL-3, author includes OCA, tests passing, OCA commit format
- Maturity levels: Alpha/Beta=1 review, Stable=2 reviews+5 days+tests, Mature=Stable+docs+changelog+2 contributors
- Don't force push after review starts. Don't squash without asking.

changelog.change: Restructured to gentle-ai standard (Output Contract, Decision Gates, Hard Rules)

skills.name: oca-governance-commit-messages
skills.title: OCA Commit Messages
skills.compact_rules:
OCA commit message format. Replaces caveman-commit for Odoo projects.
- Format: [TAG] module_name: short description (max 50 chars)
- Tags: [FIX] bug fix, [ADD] new feature, [IMP] improvement, [REF] refactoring, [REM] remove, [MIG] migration, [MOV] move, [MERGE], [DOC], [TEST], [SEC], [PERF]
- Use imperative mood: 'Fix' not 'Fixed'
- Body explains WHY not WHAT (max 80 chars/line)
- One logical change per commit
- Multi-module: [IMP] mod1, mod2: description
- Close issues: Closes #123
- No past tense, no periods in subject, no 'Fix pep8' commits

changelog.change: Added full OCA commit reference (12 tags, imperative mood, multi-module, squash rules)
Initial version with basic format

skills.name: oca-contributing-guidelines
skills.title: OCA Contributing Guidelines
skills.compact_rules:
Consolidated OCA contributing guidelines.
- Module names: singular, base_ prefix, l10n_CC_ for localization
- Files: models/<model>.py, views/<model>_views.xml
- XML IDs: <model>_view_<type>, <model>_action, <model>_menu
- Manifest: version={ver}.0.1.0.0, license=AGPL-3, author includes OCA, website=github.com/OCA/<repo>
- Import order: stdlib, third-party, odoo, addons, local, unknown with try/except
- Model order: _name/_inherit, fields, _sql_constraints, defaults, compute/search, constraints/onchange, CRUD, actions, business
- Method naming: _compute_<field>, _inverse_<field>, _search_<field>, _default_<field>, _onchange_<field>, _check_<name>, action_<name>
- Fields: Many2one=_id, One2many/Many2many=_ids, no string= if same as name
- SQL: ALWAYS use parameters %s, NEVER concatenate strings, NEVER cr.commit()
- Tests: @tagged('post_install', '-at_install'), TransactionCase, setUpClass, one test per method

skills.name: owl-components
skills.title: OWL Component Patterns
skills.compact_rules:
- OWL version: 2.x for Odoo 16-19 (bundled OWL 2.8.2 for 16-18, 2.8.4 for 19); OWL 3.x does not exist in any Odoo release
- Read target Odoo Community source before coding; Enterprise source only when applicable
- Register lifecycle hooks (onWillStart, onMounted, onWillUpdateProps, onWillUnmount) inside setup()
- Declare every child in static components; define child classes before static fields to avoid TDZ
- Use services via useService() and register components in the correct registry
- Include every OWL XML template in the correct asset bundle and order; test asset/template completeness
- Methods called through orm.call require @api.model where applicable; test the RPC path
- Odoo 18 HOOT tests use *.test.js and belong in web.assets_tests
- Reuse native Odoo components, services, Bootstrap/Odoo utilities, o_* naming, and existing design tokens; avoid parallel design systems

skills.name: odf-design
skills.title: Design Odoo Module
skills.compact_rules:
Produce a CLOSED design document (docs/design-contract.md).
- Read ASSESS REQ-XX + human EXPECTATIONS EXP-XX BEFORE designing
- Fix the target module (new vs inherited) — IMPLEMENT must not decide it
- Resolve every EXP-XX into concrete fields/models/views/security/archives
- Data model: _name/_inherit + fields (type, required, index, relation, default)
- Views: type + action + domain + menu parent. Security: ir.model.access.csv by group + ir.rule
- Derive IMPLEMENT tasks: each task references exact file(s) + EXP-XX
- Apply the closed-design checklist; if not closed -> iterate, never return ok
- IMPLEMENT consumes the design; missing decision -> reopen DESIGN, never improvise

skills.name: odf-implement
skills.title: Implement Odoo Tasks
skills.compact_rules:
Implement assigned tasks in batches following spec + closed design.
- Read REQ-XX from assess before implementing each task
- If design_closed is not true, block and reopen DESIGN; never improvise
- Follow design decisions. If wrong: NOTE IT, don't silently deviate
- Tests with code: same commit as behavior they verify
- Odoo DB tests require exact -d {test_db}; Docker: docker compose run --rm odoo odoo -d {test_db} -i {module} --test-enable --stop-after-init
- Disposable test databases are preferred; a named non-isolated development DB is allowed only for the current run when the user-approved scope names and authorizes that exact DB
- State non-isolated/user-authorized status and warn tests may mutate module, schema, and test data
- Consent to use the DB does not authorize destructive setup; separate current consent is required for the exact operation/database
- Smoke tests per batch: pre-commit + pylint-odoo on changed files
- Mark tasks [x] as you go. If blocked: status: blocked

skills.name: odf-verify
skills.title: Verify Odoo Implementation
skills.compact_rules:
Quality gate: evidence-based risk tiers + lens review + single-attempt correction budget.
- Classify tier from the FROZEN diff (never diff size): HIGH (security/perms/raw SQL/money/data-loss/subprocess/public endpoints → 4 lenses risk/resilience/readability/reliability), MEDIUM (1 lens, default readability), LOW (0 lenses: structural readback + native tools, no reviewers)
- Judgment Day 3-pass review runs ONLY for HIGH tier
- Run the real module test suite with exact -d {test_db}; record command, exact database, exit_code, and output evidence
- Disposable databases are preferred; a named non-isolated development DB is allowed only for the current run when the user-approved scope names and authorizes that exact DB
- State non-isolated/user-authorized status and warn tests may mutate module, schema, and test data
- Consent to use the DB does not authorize destructive setup; separate current consent is required for the exact operation/database
- Static analysis and manual browser checks never substitute for module tests
- User-run test evidence is valid: record via odf-toolkit manual-evidence (executor user-manual); never re-run or fabricate
- Skipped, deferred, unavailable, or unrecorded tests → blocked with verification-deferred; never PASS or PASS WITH WARNINGS
- Every REQ-XX must have a PASSING test (COMPLIANT) or it's UNTESTED (CRITICAL)
- Correction budget: min(200, ceil(original_changed_lines/2)) lines, ONE attempt, re-verify once against same frozen diff (frozen_diff_ref); inconclusive validator doesn't consume the attempt; failed → escalate to user, never auto-loop
- Never fix issues — only report. Orchestrator decides

skills.name: odf-tdd
skills.title: ODF Strict TDD
skills.compact_rules:
Strict TDD opt-in, two-source kill switch (any off wins, fail-closed).
- Effective mode = global flags.strict_tdd (registry) AND absence of local marker <worktree>/.odf/tdd.off
- Any source off → effective OFF; unreadable local → OFF (fail-closed), never ON
- Resolve effective mode BEFORE each IMPLEMENT/VERIFY phase; preflight tdd_mode is only the declared default
- Tests BEFORE code: persist a real non-zero red run before implementation; missing red evidence blocks
- Every REQ-XX must have a test task paired with implementation task
- VERIFY rejects code without matching tests when effective mode is ON
- Re-activating TDD re-validates state from zero. Global toggle: /odf-tdd on|off; local off-only marker: /odf-tdd local off|on
